text: A telephone channel has 3,100 Hz of bandwidth and an SNR of 30 dB. What is its Shannon capacity?
explanation: 30 dB is a linear ratio of 1,000, so C = 3,100 x log2(1001) = 3,100 x 9.97 = about 31 kb/s. V.34 modems achieved 28.8 and later 33.6 kb/s on good lines — right against the bound, which is why analog modem speeds stopped improving despite enormous commercial pressure.
